homeIntro: Plan tasks on your board, run checks in your local checkout, and read the logs when something fails.
homePassNote: The check finished with exit code 0. Its output stays in the run history so you can review it later.
homeFailNote: Formatting stopped this check before the tests ran. Fix the file named in the output, then submit a new check.
homeReadRun: Read a run, line by line.
homeReadIntro: The exit code tells you whether a check passed. The logs tell you why. Switch between two sample runs to see what to look for.
homeHostedQuestion: Can I run a check on the hosted website?
homeHostedAnswer: No. Checks run against your checkout on your machine. The browser runs page is only available when you start the Web development server locally; the CLI works without that server.
homeRestartQuestion: What happens if I restart the runner?
homeRestartAnswer: Completed runs and their logs stay in local SQLite history. If a check was interrupted, the runner marks it as failed on restart. Submit a new check when you’re ready to retry.
homeAccountsAnswer: Members can manage their own account settings. Administrators can also open the account directory to find a teammate and change their role. Signing up does not grant administrator access.
homePhoneQuestion: How do I connect from my phone?
homePhoneAnswer: In the Kipivo mobile app, set the workspace address to your Web or gateway address. You can test the connection, then open the workspace in your browser to sign in.
homeGuideIntro: Where your checks run, what gets saved, and how to share access.
homeRunLocallyIntro: On macOS or Linux, install the dependencies and open two terminals at the root of your trusted Kipivo checkout. Run the check and read its logs in the same terminal so the run ID stays available.
homeLocalRunsHint: Prefer the browser? With the runner active, open <link>Local runs</link> to submit a check or follow its output.
commandsCopyFailed: Select the command to copy it manually.
